cite_as: Bos, J. M., Dhillon, S., & Borman, T. (2019). Building Assets and Reducing Risks (BARR) Validation Study: Final Report. American Institutes for Research (ERIC ED602462).

cite_as: Faria, A.-M., Sorensen, N., Heppen, J., Bowdon, J., et al. (2017). Getting Students on Track for Graduation: Impacts of the Early Warning Intervention and Monitoring System after One Year (REL 2017-272). Regional Educational Laboratory Midwest.

cite_as: Sletten, M. A., Toge, A. G., & Malmberg-Heimonen, I. (2022). Effects of an Early Warning System on Student Absence and Completion in Norwegian Upper Secondary Schools: A Cluster-Randomised Study. Scandinavian Journal of Educational Research.
claimed_component: Design: cluster-randomized trial in 42 Norwegian upper secondary schools. Outcomes: absence and completion. Direction: no significant effects.

cite_as: Lass, K., Walsh, S., Burgess, K., et al. (2025). Evaluation of Achievement Mentoring: Final Impact Evaluation Report. Policy & Research Group (ERIC ED676904).
claimed_component: Design: randomized trial of 393 grade 10-11 students with prior-year risk flags in five Eastern states. Outcomes from school records: attendance, credits, suspensions; whether graduation or dropout was measured. Direction and sizes of each.

cite_as: Hemelt, S. W., Lenard, M. A., & Paeplow, C. G. (2019). Building Bridges to Life after High School: Contemporary Career Academies and Student Outcomes. Economics of Education Review 68, 161-178 (CALDER Working Paper 176, 2017; ERIC ED572934).
claimed_component: Design: lottery-based admission to one technology-focused career academy in Wake County, NC. Outcomes: high school graduation and ninth-grade absences. Direction and size: graduation up about 8 percentage points, concentrated among males; ninth-grade absences reduced.

cite_as: Neild, R. C., Boccanfuso, C., & Byrnes, V. (2015). Academic Impacts of Career and Technical Schools: A Case Study of a Large Urban School District. Career and Technical Education Research, 40(1), 28-47.
claimed_component: Design: comparison of admitted and not-admitted applicants to School District of Philadelphia CTE high schools (state whether admission was by lottery or selection and how applicants were compared). cite_as: Plasman, J., Stein, M. L., Durham, R. E., & Smith-Onyewu, Z. (2025). CTE Mechanisms: The Effects of Career and Technical Education Center Admissions Offers in Baltimore. Educational Evaluation and Policy Analysis.
claimed_component: Design: regression discontinuity at the admission cut score for Baltimore CTE high schools. Outcomes: attendance, CTE pathway completion, GPA, SAT, and graduation if reported. Direction: more likely to complete a CTE pathway, lower GPAs; report any graduation estimate.

cite_as: Wills, T. W., Wolford, T. E., & Goldberg, A. (2017). Effects of Career and Technical Education on Graduation Rates: A Longitudinal Study from the School District of Philadelphia. AERA paper (ERIC ED603343).
claimed_component: Design: longitudinal regression on the 2011-12 first-time ninth-grade cohort in Philadelphia, controlling for academic, behavioral and demographic factors (state whether prior achievement and attendance are among them). Outcome: four-year graduation. Direction and size: CTE participation associated with higher graduation.

cite_as: Glennie, E., Dalton, B., Studley, R., & Lauff, E. (2025). The Influence of Earning Industry Certifications on High School Graduation: Evidence from Florida. Educational Policy (ERIC EJ1476967).
claimed_component: Design: name the quasi-experimental method and whether it adjusts for prior achievement. Population: Florida high school students. Outcome: on-time graduation. Direction and size: earning certifications raises the likelihood of on-time graduation, more for at-risk and economically disadvantaged students.

cite_as: Castellano, M. E., Richardson, G. B., Sundell, K., & Stone, J. R. III (2017). Preparing Students for College and Career in the United States: The Effects of Career-Themed Programs of Study on High School Performance. Vocations and Learning, 10, 47-70 (ERIC EJ1133891).
claimed_component: Design: longitudinal study in two districts using an instrumental-variable or lottery-based estimate. Outcome: progress toward graduation or graduation, plus GPA and test scores. Direction and size for the graduation-related outcome.

cite_as: Furstenberg, F. F., Jr., & Neumark, D. (2007). Encouraging Education in an Urban School District: Evidence from the Philadelphia Educational Longitudinal Study. Education Economics, 15(2), 135-157 (ERIC EJ764115; NBER WP 11260).

cite_as: Berger, A., Turk-Bicakci, L., Garet, M., Song, M., Knudson, J., Haxton, C., et al. (2013). Early College, Early Success: Early College High School Initiative Impact Study. American Institutes for Research (ERIC ED577243).
claimed_component: Design: admission-lottery randomized comparison at early college high schools. Outcome: high school graduation (and state ELA tests). Direction and size: early college students more likely to graduate; report percentages.

cite_as: Edmunds, J. A., Unlu, F., Glennie, E., Bernstein, L., Fesler, L., Furey, J., & Arshavsky, N. (2016). The Small, Stand-Alone Early College: Impact on High School Outcomes. SREE (ERIC ED567039).
claimed_component: Design: lottery-based randomized study of North Carolina early college high schools. Outcome: high school graduation. Direction and size: positive impact on graduation.

cite_as: Maxwell, N., Bellotti, J., Schochet, P., Burkander, P., Whitesell, E., Dillon, E., Inanc, H., Geckeler, C., & Gonzalez, R. (2019). Building College and Career Pathways for High School Students: Youth CareerConnect. Mathematica for the U.S. Department of Labor (WWC study 90317).
claimed_component: Design: randomized trial of Youth CareerConnect career-focused learning. Outcomes: enrolled in high school, unexcused absences, credentials. Direction: no significant effects.

cite_as: Theodos, B., Pergamit, M. R., Hanson, D., Edelstein, S., Daniels, R., & Srini, T. (2016/2017). Embarking on College and Career: Interim and Final Evaluation of Urban Alliance. Urban Institute (ERIC ED570478).
claimed_component: Design: randomized trial of the Urban Alliance paid internship, training and mentoring for high school seniors in DC and Baltimore. Outcome: high school graduation. Direction and size of the graduation estimate.

cite_as: Constantine, J. M., Seftor, N. S., Martin, E. S., Silva, T., & Myers, D. (2006). Study of the Effect of the Talent Search Program on Secondary and Postsecondary Outcomes in Florida, Indiana and Texas. U.S. Department of Education (ERIC ED493358).
claimed_component: Design: matched comparison (WWC: meets standards with reservations). Outcome: earned a high school diploma or GED. Direction: no significant effect on high school completion as reviewed by WWC.

cite_as: Todhunter-Reid, A., Burke, A., Houchens, P., Howard, M., et al. (2020). AVID Participation in High School and Post-Secondary Success: An Evaluation and Cost Analysis. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness.
claimed_component: Design: coarsened exact matching on about 40 covariates including prior achievement. Outcome: high school graduation. Direction and size: students completing at least one AVID elective had higher graduation.

cite_as: Sepanik, S., Safran, S., & Saco, L. (2018). Building College Readiness across Rural Communities: Implementation and Outcome Findings for the AVID Central Florida Collaborative Study. MDRC (ERIC ED582154).
claimed_component: Design: comparative interrupted time series of schoolwide AVID. Outcomes: graduation, credits earned, ELA tests, advanced courses. Direction: little difference in graduation and credits.

cite_as: Kim, H., Montague, M. L., & Castillo, L. G. (2025). The Effects of Gaining Early Awareness and Readiness for Undergraduate Programs on Educational Outcomes: A Meta-Analysis. Journal of Diversity in Higher Education.
claimed_component: Design: meta-analysis of GEAR UP evaluations; the share of included studies with a comparison group and the designs used. Outcome: high school graduation rate. Direction and size.

cite_as: Miller, C., Cummings, D., Millenky, M., Wiegand, A., & Long, D. (2018). Laying a Foundation: Four-Year Results from the National YouthBuild Evaluation. MDRC.
claimed_component: Design: randomized trial at about 75 programs. Population: out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24. Outcome: high school diploma or equivalency (state the split between diploma and GED). Direction and size.

cite_as: Millenky, M., Bloom, D., & Dillon, C. (2010). Making the Transition: Interim Results of the National Guard Youth ChalleNGe Evaluation. MDRC (ERIC ED514652).
claimed_component: Design: randomized trial. Population: 16-18-year-olds who had left school. Outcome: earned a diploma or GED. Direction and size; whether gains were mainly GEDs.

cite_as: Cave, G., Bos, H., Doolittle, F., & Toussaint, C. (1993). JOBSTART: Final Report on a Program for School Dropouts. MDRC (ERIC ED363774).
claimed_component: Design: randomized trial. Population: school dropouts. Outcome: earned a high school diploma or GED within 48 months. Direction and size.

cite_as: Riccio, J., Dechausay, N., Miller, C., Nunez, S., Verma, N., & Yang, E. (2013). Conditional Cash Transfers in New York City: The Continuing Story of the Opportunity NYC-Family Rewards Demonstration. MDRC.
claimed_component: Design: randomized trial of about 4,800 families. Outcomes for high school students: credits, Regents exams, graduation. Direction: which high school outcomes improved (overall or only for students proficient at entry) and whether graduation changed.

cite_as: Miller, C., Riccio, J., et al. (2016-2017). Effects of a Modified Conditional Cash Transfer Program in Two American Cities: Findings from Family Rewards 2.0. MDRC.
claimed_component: Design: randomized trial in the Bronx and Memphis. Outcome: high school progress (credits, on-track or graduation). Direction: no effect on school progress through Year 4, for the full sample or the proficient subgroup.

cite_as: Long, D., Gueron, J. M., Wood, R. G., Fisher, R., & Fellerath, V. (1996). LEAP: Three-Year Impacts of Ohio's Welfare Initiative to Improve School Attendance among Teenage Parents. MDRC (ERIC ED396380).
